full_judgment:
Constitution. this Rule nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 issued under Section 3 or the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (to he called Ordinance, 1982) arising out of L.A. Case 

 3. However, all on a sudden the petitioners have been received the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 (Annexure-A) showing their homestead land has been proposed to be acquired for the purpose of extension of an Agro based industry namely "Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Limited". Having learnt about that notice (Annexure-A) the petitioners collected the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the above named company; from which it revealed that the said company is a private limited company registered under the Companies Act, 1994. Then the petitioners jointly filed an application before the respondent No. 4 on 07.05.2012 (Annexure-0) with a prayer not to acquire the land in question on the ground that the land is homestead and the petitioners are living thereon and they have no other land to live. It was further stated that if the land is acquired for the purpose of enlargement of a private limited company the petitioners will be suffered from irreparable loss and injury and they will be thrown out from their homestead. 

 4. Upon received the said application the respondent No.4, the land acquisition Officer issued a letter dated 13.05.2012 (Annexure H) directing the petitioners to appear before the respondent No. 1 i.e. the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla with the necessary papers and documents to redress their grievances, Accordingly the petitioners attended the said office of the respondent No.1 and agitated the same grievances as raised in their objection (Annexure-G). But unfortunately the respondent No.1 in a most arbitrary and unlawful manner informed the petitioners that there is no other alternative but to acquire the land in question as the local administration is under tremendous pressure from the local member of Parliament, In the said compelling circumstances the petitioners were constrained to file this writ petition challenging the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 (Annexure-A) and thereby obtained the present rule. 

 5. The respondent No.1 & 3 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverted the material allegations made in the writ petition and contended inter-alia that the land as proposed to be acquired has been taken under consideration for acquisition for the purpose of establishment of an Agro based industries for the benefit of general people of the locality and that was done for the public interest also; as there will be an opportunity of employment of thousands of workers and staffs who will be involved in the food processing works for exporting the same in abroad. It further asserted by the respondents that the Managing Director of the Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Company Limited forwarded a letter of requisition to the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla vide their memo No. Cha.Fa.0.189/12 dated 25.03.2012 in order to acquisition of 0.30 acres of land of B.S. Plot No. 450, situated under Mouza- Dotola Gobindapur to use the same for the purpose of different infrastructures in response to the need of the extension work of the said Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage which have been engaged in service of the food - processing works and exporting the same regularly to the abroad. Al the same lime there is a Master Plan awaiting to be executed to the aim and view of extension of the said industries in order to storage food grain of the locality and also to undertake production of export oriented goods in large scale in the long run. 

 6. In response to the said proposal of the Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Limited the District Land Acquisition and Allocation Committee have taken a decision in a meeting held on 08.04.2012 and after threadbare discussions the committee found there is no legal impediment to acquire the proposed 0.30 acres of land from plot No. 450 and accordingly the acquiring authority initiated the L.A. Case No. 7/2011-12 arcl thereby notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 was served upon the petitioners and other concerned parties of the locality. The notices were also duly served upon the original owners of the land, namely Parimal Chandra Acharia. Gupal Chandra Acharia. Srinath Bhowmic and others on 24.04.2012. Thereafter in presence of the members of the requiring organization, officials of the government authority and also the petitioners and upon holding spot inquiry the list of structures trees and plants standing thereon were made on account and thereby the valuation of the land, structures and trees were assessed, properly. Then the notice recipients namely (I) Nilofa Begum and (2) Rahima Khatoon subMitted their objections under Section 4(1) of the Ordinance and accordingly the said objections were heard and disposed of observing that since the project is mainly engaged in producing exportable food items and exports the same in abroad regularly and now the agro based organization in need to be extended in order to undertake production of its large scale exportable items and upon consideration of the said public and national interest the authority concerned rejected the objections raised by the aforesaid two objectors. Thereafter the proposal of acquisition was forwarded to the Divisional Commissioner for his consideration under Section 5(I) of the Ordinance. 1982 and accordingly the Divisional Commissioner sent back the proposal to the local authority with his comments vide memo No. 665 dated 27.06.2012 and the process of acquisition is still in continuation; and thus, the attempt of the petitioners' seeking relief under Article 102 of the Constitution in challenging the notice issued tinder Section 43 of the Ordinance is barred by Section 44 of the Ordinance 1982. 

 7. When the matter appeared in the list for hearing for a couple of days, one of the day, on 30.04.2015 Mr. Mukunda Chandra Debnath, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the respondents issued the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 under Section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 to acquire the petitioners homestead land which is in violation of the provisions and spirit of the ordinance, 1982. He further submits that the respondents with a mala-fide intention issued the notice of acquisition for the benefit of the requiring body who is a Private Limited Company though it is an agro based industries but its ownerships belongs to a private limited company whose shares are owned by the private persons and the acquisition process as initiated is neither for a public propose nor in public interest. As such, the impugned acquisition notice was being served by the respondents to acquire the petitioners homestead is to be declared void ahinitio. He also submits that -the right to enjoyment of the property is the fundamental right of every citizens of Bangladesh which has been guaranteed by our constitution. However by issuing the impugned notice in violation of the relevant laws the respondents have infringed the fundamental right of the petitioners and if so the proposed acquisition is held the petitioner will he thrown out form their homestead. Therefore he prayed for making the rule absolute by declaring the impugned acquisition notice issued by the respondents is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 8. On the other hand Mr. Mahbubey Alam. the learned Attorney General appearing with 10 Mr. Bishowjit Roy and Mr. Md. Ekramul Hoque, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 submits that the land in question was proposed to be acquired for public purpose: as because the proposed industries wherein thousands of people of the locality are supposed to be employed. He further submits that the local harvests mainly potato and other food grains are produced in the said locality in a large scale and if the proposed cold storage he established the agro based crops and harvests production will be protected and the local farmer and inhabitants of the locality will he benefited at large. Therefore, he emphasis on his submissions that the proposed acquisition notice was served for public purpose as well as in public interest. The learned Attorney General referring to a decision, the ease of Razab Ali and others -Vs- Province of East Pakistan and others, reported in 12 DLR-524, submits that though by the proposed acquisition process the requiring body being a private company will have to be benefited but ultimately it will serve it large number of public of the locality by protecting their agro products and also by creating an scope of employment of thousands of people of the locality. As such, the acquisition as proposed was made for a public purpose and is valid under the law. 

 9. On our query, is there any agreement executed by the requiring body with the acquiring authority as mandated under Section 15 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance. 1982 before serving notice tinder Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982? The learned Attorney General referring to a decision the case of Mrinalendu Pal -Vs- Divisional Commissioner and others, reported in 2 = BLC(1997)- 495 submits that since the petitioner failed to agitate their grievances in this regard in filing their objection before the acquiring authority under Section 4 of the Ordinance or in their writ petition, the respondents are in a position having no opportunity to controvert the same. As such, the said argument cannot be agitated at this stage of hearing of the rule. The learned Attorney General lastly submits that having though the above two established decisions, more so, our apex Court in the case of Abdus Salam -Vs-Government of Bangladesh reported in 5 MLR(AD)-184 has decided if the acquisition notices issued for public purpose it cannot be challenged under Article 102 of the Constitution. The present petitioners being failed to maintain the legal requirements as enunciated in 2 BLC Case they cannot challenge the notice issued under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 at this stage for non-compliance of proposition of Section 15 of the said Ordinance. The learned Attorney General mainly emphasis to his submissions on the point that the property in question as being proposed to be acquired for a public purpose as well as in public interest, therefore the notice issued under Section 3 of the Ordinance cannot be said it is null and void. Furthermore, he referring to Section 44 of the Ordinance, 1982 submits that the law itself debarred any party to file any suit or any application in respect of any order passed or any action taken or to be taken in pursuance of any power conferred under this ordinance. Thus, he urges for discharging the rule. 

 11. It further appears from the annexure, those have been annexed to the respondents affidavit-in-opposition. particularly from Annexure-1 series, it shows that the Board of Investment which is being under the office of the Prime Minister, in approving the project "Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Limited" vide its letter dated 20.04.2011 specifically mentioned and requested the respondent No.1, the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla to submit a full report with its opinion in acquiring 2.23 acres of private land in favour of the aforesaid project other than contrary to the acquisition of the land such as homestead, roads or high ways, school, college, mosque, madrasha, temple or other  religions structures and having any legal disputes or suits involves thereon. The Deputy Commissioner, Comilla then following such directives of the Board of Investment, vide its Memo dated 28.04.2011 asked the Assistant Commissioner (Land), the respondent No. 3 herein, to sent a report after holding spot investigation to the said 2.23 acres of land as proposed to be acquired for the purpose of Chandina Farmland and stating in the report in detail' whether there remains any homestead or other religious structures and legal disputes or suits as contrary to the acquisition. Accordingly, in response to that letter of respondent No. 1, the respondent 3 vide its memo dated 09.05.2011 submitted a report categorically mentioning therein that the land in question though was recorded as vested property but ultimately under the V.P. Case No. 38 of 1997 and 77 of 1998, the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla vide its memo No. ৭২৫/১(৩)কুম/ভিপি dated 30.08.1999 released 0.30 acres of land in favour of the petitioner Rahima Khatun and one Harunur Rashid and on the said 0.30 acres of land they are residing there by erecting their houses. The respondent No.3 in the said report specifically mentioned "প্রতিবেদন পযালোচনায় আরো দেখা যায় যে সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক আবেদীত ৪৪৮ (এস এস ১৫৯) দাগের ০.৬১ একর ভূমি নিয়ে দেওয়ানী ১১৩/২০১০ নং মামলা চলমান থাকলেও বসতবাড়ি রাস্তাঘাট স্কুল কলেজ মসজিদ মাদ্রাসা মন্দির গীর্জা বা অন্যকোন স্থাপনা নেই এবং আবেদীত ৪৫০ (এস এ ১৫২) দাগের ০.০৩ একর ভূমিতে বসতবাড়ী ব্যতিত রাস্তা অন্যকোন স্থাপনা নেই।” (Under lined to emphasis). 

 12. Upon going through the above spot inquiry report of the respondent No. 3 (Annexure-I series), it reveals that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Chandina intelligently made his report stating that in 0.61 acres of land though there is a suit being No. 113 of 2010 is pending but there is no homestead or religious structures, simultaneously in respect of 0.30 acres of land (i.e. the land in question) other than homestead there is no roads or high ways. School, Mosque, Mdrasha, Temple and other religious structures remains thereon. It is very interesting that on the prayer of the requiring body, "Chandian Farmland and Cold Storage Limited", the Board of Investment in approving the said project by their letter dated 20.04.2011 categorically asked the respondent No. 1 to submit a report mentioning as to the proposed private land may not contrary to the acquisition having there remains any homestead, religious structures and soil or legal disputes. However, it shows from the report dated 09.05.2011 submitted by the respondent No.3, on the query of respondent No. I. that a suit being No. 113 of 2010 is pending relating to the proposed 0.61 acres of land and on the 0.30 acres of land as proposed to be acquired, the petitioner No.1 Rahima Khatun and one Harunur Rashid are residing with their family members by erecting their houses thereon for long time. Having such assertions though have been made in the spot investigation report but disregarding such spot inquiry report and disobeying the query of the Board of Investment the present respondents proceeded with the acquisition proceedings vide L.A. Case No. 7/2011-12 by issuing the impugned notices under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 and proposed to acquire the petitioners' homestead land and also is going to take further action under Section 5 of the Ordinance. 1982 which is very much contrary to the letter of the Board of Investment dated 20.04.2011 and also as of the letter of respondent No. I dated 28.04.2011 who requested the respondent No. 3 to submit a spot inquiry report re-iterating the anxiety of the Board of Investment as to whether the proposed private lands are in contrary to the acquisition. 

 13. Moreover, in acquiring land for any person other than the government the Section 15 of the Ordinance, 1982 imposed a precondition of agreement before serving notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982. For proper disposal of the rule we may reproduce or quote here the said Section IS of the Acquisition & Requisition of Immovable Property Act, 1982, which runs as follows: 

 14. From the above provisions of law it transpires that the acquiring authority i.e. the government in acquisition of a property in favour of the requiring body who is a private person or a private entity other than the government, the said requiring body shall have to execute an agreement with the government before issuance of the notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance. But on our query either the petitioner or the respondents failed to show us any of such agreement as has been executed by the requiring body with the acquiring authority; though admittedly the requiring body is firmly found as a private limited company whose shares are belonging to some private persons. 

 "Section 15 is a mandatory provision of law to be complied with by the requiring body before the acquiring authority proceeds for acquisition of the land if such acquisition is made not for public purposes of the Government". 

 "The purpose for entering in to such agreement is to initiate the process of acquisition so that the person on whose favour the land will be acquired gets possession from the Government on payment of compensation. The obligation of the requiring body under the agreement is to deposit compensation money within time specified therein and the obligation of the acquiring authority is to acquire the land after performance of formalities and then to handover possession to the requiring body. If the latter does not deposit the compensation money within the specified time, the acquiring authority will not be able to pay the compensation to the affected person under Section 10 and if the compensation is not paid the Deputy Commissioner has no power to take possession from the affected person. The payment of compensation is a precondition for taking over possession of the land. Thus there is no scope on the part of the acquiring authority to complete the process of acquisition as per provisions of the Ordinance unless the requiring body deposits the compensation money as per agreement." 

 17. In reliance to the above two decisions we are unable to accept the submissions advanced by the learned Attorney General referring to the decision reported in 2 BLC-495 and the decision reported in 12 DLR-524 which does not overcome the query of this Court; as it appears that the judgment reported in 12 DLR-524 was passed before enactment of the Ordinance, 1982 and also before coming into force of Section 15 of that Ordinance. In acquisition of a property in favour of the requiring body who is a private person other than the government, the mandatory provision of agreement is to be executed by the requiring body before issuance of notice under Section-3 as mandated by Section 15 of the Ordinance-1982. Which is not a factual aspect to be rebut but a legal proposition and that should be maintained by the respondent government who being the acquiring authority and they are bound to follow the requirement of law enunciated in the statute and they should have to follow the same before issuance of the notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982. However, in the present case we do not find any such agreement executed by the requiring body though admittedly the acquisition process was started though L.A. Case No. 7/2011-12 in favour and for the benefit of a private limited company. 

 Of course, there is no doubt that the purpose of acquisition was for the public purpose and of public interest also, as the local people and farmers of the locality will be benefited by the expansion of Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Limited and there will he an opportunity of employment of thousands of people. 

 18. But it is unfortunate that the acquiring authority i.e. the present respondents disregarding the spot inquiry report and the mandatory Provisions of Law proceeded with the acquisition process by infringing the petitioners' fundamental right of housing: though the petitioner or the respondents failed to show before this Court any of such agreement as to he executed by the requiring body with the acquiring authority before serving notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance as provided by Section 15 of the said Ordinance. 1982, since having admittedly the requiring body „, is a private limited company.
